resources.string:
1. Open Scan from the bottom navigation.

2. Take a photo of a banana leaf or choose a photo from your gallery. BananaQ analyzes the image.

3. Review the detected condition, confidence, and available recommendations.

4. Open History to revisit saved scans. Use the Disease Library on Home to explore the supported conditions.

1. Open Scan and allow camera access when prompted.

2. Frame one banana leaf clearly and tap the capture button. You can also use the gallery button to select an existing photo.

3. Keep the app open while the image is analyzed.

4. Review the result. If the image cannot be assessed or the result is uncertain, take another photo with better lighting and focus.

The result shows the predicted condition and a confidence score. Confidence describes how strongly the model favors its prediction; it does not guarantee that the diagnosis is correct.

Review the condition information alongside the visible signs on the leaf. The app supports Healthy, Black Sigatoka, Panama Disease, and Cordana Leaf Spot.

An uncertain result is a reason to retake the photo. A Healthy result does not rule out every plant problem. Seek advice from an agricultural professional if symptoms persist or the result does not match what you observe.

After a scan, open the Treatment tab in the condition details to review the recommendations. Read the condition information first so you understand which result the guidance relates to.

You can also explore a condition through the Disease Library on Home.

Recommendations are general guidance. Confirm the plant problem with an agricultural professional before choosing a treatment, especially when the scan is uncertain.

Open the Prevention tab in the condition details after a scan or through the Disease Library.

Use this section to learn about reducing the risk of future problems. Revisit the guidance when checking your plants and watch for changes in leaf appearance.

For advice suited to your farm and local conditions, consult an agricultural professional.

• Use bright, even light. Avoid harsh shadows and glare.

• Hold the camera steady and make sure the leaf is in focus.

• Frame one banana leaf against a simple background. Keep the affected area clearly visible.

• Avoid covering the leaf with fingers or other leaves.

• Use an original, clear photo without filters. Retake the photo if it is blurry, too dark, or too far away.
